_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

notes: A personal token is the simpler path for one workspace and is what Flux offers first; OAuth is for connecting more than one account or for a build shared with other people.
read_only is requested deliberately. read_write on a payments account means an agent could create charges and refunds, and no task in the catalogue needs that.
The token endpoint is on connect.stripe.com, not api.stripe.com. The api.stripe.com/v1/oauth/token form appears in older material and is the wrong host.
This is Stripe Connect OAuth, for reaching an account you do not own. Reading your own account only needs a restricted API key.

personal_token.label: Restricted API key
personal_token.where: dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys - create a restricted key with read permissions only on customers, invoices, payments and subscriptions.
notes: Use a restricted key, never the secret key. A restricted key with read-only permissions cannot move money even if it leaks.

rate_limits.note: Around 100 read requests per second in live mode, less in test. Search endpoints are lower. Returns 429.

notes: The search corrected an assumption: the token endpoint is connect.stripe.com/oauth/token, not api.stripe.com/v1/oauth/token.
API version read out of stripe-python's _api_version.py, which is generated from Stripe's OpenAPI spec. The 2024-06-20 I first wrote was two years stale.
